Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},

 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},

                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),

   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?

   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?

   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?

}

result.name: Synopsys, Inc.
result.industry: Electronic design automation (EDA) software, semiconductor IP and engineering simulation
markets: Electronic design automation (chip design, verification and signoff software)
Semiconductor design IP (interface and foundation IP)
Engineering simulation and analysis (Ansys multiphysics: HFSS, Fluent, Mechanical)

mission.statement: Our Mission is to Empower Innovators to Drive Human Advancement
mission.source: Synopsys company website (synopsys.com/company) and FY2025 Form 10-K (Human Capital Resources section)
mission.plain: Synopsys builds the tools that let engineers invent the chips and machines that move people forward.

about.plain: Synopsys makes the computer programs that engineers use to design computer chips. A modern chip has billions of tiny switches, far too many to draw by hand, so engineers use Synopsys software to plan, check and test the chip before it is made. It also sells ready-made chip building blocks, like the parts that let a chip talk to memory or USB, so customers do not have to design them from scratch. Since buying Ansys in July 2025, it also sells software that simulates how cars, planes and phones behave in the real world.
about.customers: Chip companies like NVIDIA, Intel and Samsung, plus makers of phones, cars, planes and other complex products.
about.everyday: The chip inside your phone, laptop or game console was very likely designed and checked with Synopsys software before it was ever built.

money.plain: software to design, check and test chips (FY2025 Design Automation segment excluding Ansys)
ready-made, pre-tested chip parts like USB, PCIe, DDR/HBM memory and die-to-die links
physics simulation of heat, airflow, stress and radio waves; only about 3.5 months in FY2025 ($756.6M), expected about $2.9B in FY2026
ZeBu emulators and HAPS prototyping boxes that run a chip design before it is built
Synopsys.ai and 'agentic' AI engineers, including a 2026 revenue-sharing deal with OpenAI to build an AI model for chip design

result.summary: Synopsys has a wide moat: it and Cadence form a near-duopoly in chip design software (about 31% and 30% of the EDA market in 2024 per TrendForce), customers are locked in by years of trained engineers, scripts and foundry-certified flows, and its IP portfolio is the largest outside Arm. The Ansys deal added the leading multiphysics simulation franchise, though it also added about $10B of debt and integration risk, and FY2025 showed the IP business can stumble (export curbs and a weak foundry customer).

pricingPower.evidence: Gross margin has stayed near 77-80% for years (77.0% in FY2025 GAAP), the Design Automation segment earned a 45.2% adjusted operating margin in Q3 FY2026, multi-year time-based licences renew with year-end backlog of $11.4B (FY2025), and management targets ~50% non-GAAP operating margin by FY2030 without losing volume.

moats.evidence: Tools like PrimeTime (timing signoff), Fusion Compiler, VCS and Ansys HFSS/Fluent are industry 'golden' references, backed by decades of patents and foundry certifications at TSMC, Samsung and Intel.

Chip teams build flows, scripts and sign-off methodologies around Synopsys tools on multi-year licences; a failed tape-out at advanced nodes can cost tens of millions, so customers rarely swap vendors mid-stream.
Foundries co-develop process design kits with Synopsys and Cadence first, and the large pool of engineers trained on Synopsys tools makes them the default choice for new hires and IP partners.
R&D spending of more than 25% of roughly $9B of revenue (company website) is far beyond what EDA startups or Chinese rivals can fund, and IP blocks are amortised over thousands of customer chips.

The EDA market is small relative to its importance and is shared mainly by Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens (about 74% combined in 2024 per TrendForce), leaving little room for a profitable new full-flow entrant.
Synopsys is an incumbent; AI-native design startups could counter-position, though Synopsys is pre-empting them with Synopsys.ai and agentic AI work.
Nearly 40 years of algorithm refinement in synthesis, place-and-route and signoff, tuned node by node with foundries, is very hard to replicate.
Synopsys employs one of the largest pools of EDA R&D engineers (about 28,000 staff at FY2025 year-end before a planned ~10% cut), but talent is not exclusive and Cadence competes for the same people.

customers.evidence: Synopsys does not publish NPS or renewal rates, but backlog reached $11.4B at FY2025 year-end and leading chipmakers such as NVIDIA (which also invested $2B in December 2025) and AWS (a multi-year IP licence worth over $1B announced in 2026) deepened ties; a major foundry customer's troubles hurt IP sales in FY2025.

talent.evidence: Synopsys was named to the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For list in 2026, but a restructuring approved in November 2025 is cutting about 10% of the workforce after the Ansys deal.

product.evidence: Synopsys claims the #1 position in EDA for advanced-node designs, in interface and foundation IP, and (via Ansys) in multiphysics simulation; its PrimeTime and Fusion Compiler flows are used on most leading-edge chips.

competitors.name: Cadence Design Systems
competitors.note: The other half of the EDA duopoly: digital/analog design, verification, emulation (Palladium), design IP and system simulation.

competitors.name: Siemens (Siemens EDA, Altair)
competitors.note: Siemens EDA (formerly Mentor) leads physical verification with Calibre; its Altair purchase added simulation that overlaps Ansys.

competitors.name: Keysight Technologies
competitors.note: RF and high-speed EDA (PathWave/ADS); bought Synopsys's divested Optical Solutions Group and PowerArtist after the Ansys deal.

competitors.name: Dassault Systèmes
competitors.note: SIMULIA simulation competes with Ansys in structural, fluids and electromagnetic analysis.

competitors.name: Arm Holdings
competitors.note: Largest design IP vendor (processor IP and compute subsystems); competes for IP budgets though not in interface IP.

competitors.name: Rambus
competitors.note: Memory and security interface IP such as HBM and PCIe controllers.

competitors.name: Empyrean Technology
competitors.note: China's leading domestic EDA vendor, backed by government push for self-sufficiency.

competitors.name: Primarius Technologies
competitors.note: Chinese EDA vendor in device modelling and circuit simulation.

competitors.name: COMSOL
competitors.note: Private multiphysics simulation software competing with Ansys tools.

competitors.name: Silvaco Group
competitors.note: TCAD, analog/custom EDA and some IP.

competitors.name: CEVA
competitors.note: DSP, wireless connectivity and AI processor IP.

threats: US-China export controls: BIS curbed EDA sales to China in May 2025 (later lifted) and China was about 16% of FY2024 revenue; renewed curbs or Chinese self-sufficiency (Empyrean, Primarius) could cut sales.
Customer concentration and foundry health: troubles at a major foundry customer hurt Design IP in FY2025.
Cadence's aggressive push into simulation and IP, and Siemens's Altair deal, intensify head-to-head competition.
AI-native design startups and large customers' in-house tools could erode pricing if AI makes chip design far more automated.
Ansys integration risk, about $10.0B of debt (July 2026) and a ~10% workforce cut could distract the organisation.
Large customers (NVIDIA, hyperscalers) designing their own flows or bargaining harder as they consolidate.

ceo.name: Sassine Ghazi
ceo.background: Electrical engineer (BSEE Georgia Tech, MSEE University of Tennessee, business degree from Lebanese American University); started as an Intel design engineer and spent 25+ years at Synopsys, including as COO, before becoming CEO.

c1.evidence: Synopsys leads EDA (about 31% share in 2024 per TrendForce), an essential but mature industry; growth is driven by AI chips rather than by the industry being new.

c2.evidence: Customers choose Synopsys for foundry-certified, best-in-class signoff and synthesis tools plus the broadest interface IP catalogue, an advantage built over decades and protected by high switching costs.

c3.evidence: Synopsys is the default leader among chip engineers but ordinary consumers rarely know the name.

c4.evidence: Its mission 'to Empower Innovators to Drive Human Advancement' is emphasised in filings and its website, and enabling the world's chips for a decade would matter, but management communication centres on margin and EPS targets.

c6.evidence: “chip design software, essential, technical” — mostly positive among engineers and investors, though few outside the industry know it.

c7.evidence: AI, data-center and automotive chips plus 'silicon to systems' simulation are expanding its market; management targets about 15% revenue CAGR from FY2026 to FY2030.

c8.evidence: The $35B Ansys acquisition moved it into system-level simulation for cars, aerospace and industrial products, and AI agent tools could open new markets.

m1.evidence: Ghazi has a clear 'silicon to systems' and AI-agent vision and executed the Ansys deal, but he is a pragmatic operator rather than a famous visionary.

m2.evidence: Ghazi is not a founder but has spent more than 25 years at Synopsys; the long-term strategy (Ansys, AI) suggests owner-like thinking.

m4.evidence: No strong public evidence either way on servant leadership; the company made the 2026 Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For list while cutting about 10% of jobs.

m5.evidence: Synopsys keeps inventing (Synopsys.ai, multi-die and AI agents), but this culture was largely built by co-founder Aart de Geus over three decades.

m6.evidence: Ghazi is an electrical engineer who began as an Intel chip designer and led Synopsys's EDA business before becoming CEO.

m7.evidence: No controversies are known, but there is little public evidence of a cause beyond the company's mission.

m7b.evidence: No commencement speech by Sassine Ghazi at a top university was found.

m8b.evidence: Ghazi keeps a low-key, engineer-executive profile with no widely known public persona.

m9.evidence: He closed the $35B Ansys deal and raised FY2026 guidance to $9.69-9.74B revenue, but FY2025 included a guidance cut and a share drop of almost 27% in the week after weak Q3 FY2025 IP results (September 2025).

m10.evidence: Synopsys is not known for frugality, though the post-Ansys restructuring cuts about 10% of staff and targets ~50% non-GAAP operating margin.

c10.evidence: Its tools indirectly improve billions of lives by enabling chips in phones, cars and data centers, but its customers are engineers, not the public.

p2.evidence: Designing and verifying chips with tens of billions of transistors at 3nm and below is extremely hard and vital to AI, computing and communications.

f1.evidence: Revenue rose every year from $3,685.3M in FY2020 to $7,054.2M in FY2025 (FY2022 onward on a continuing-operations basis after the 2024 Software Integrity sale).

f2.evidence: GAAP operating margin rose from 16.8% (FY2020) to 24.9% (FY2022) but fell to 13.0% in FY2025 after Ansys amortisation and deal costs, and gross margin slipped from 78.4% to 77.0%.

f3.evidence: Equity is positive, but debt of $10,037.4M against cash of $3,607.7M (July 31, 2026) after the Ansys deal is high, though covered by FY2026 guided operating cash flow of about $2.8B.

f4.evidence: Operating cash flow grew from $991.3M (FY2020) to $1,518.6M (FY2025) and operating income from $620.1M to $914.9M, but both peaked earlier (OCF $1,738.9M in FY2022, operating income $1,355.7M in FY2024).

v1.evidence: Synopsys and Cadence are close rivals; Synopsys is the leader in synthesis, timing signoff and interface IP, but there is no single reason an outsider would see it as clearly better than Cadence.

v2.evidence: It made the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For list in 2026, but is not a household-name employer brand and is cutting about 10% of staff.

c5.evidence: If Synopsys vanished, chipmakers from NVIDIA to Apple and carmakers using Ansys simulation would struggle to design products, delaying new phones, AI chips and cars.
